diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the same table twice with sequential scans (nodes 0 and 1), each reading all rows and applying filters afterward, then deduplicates ~198K combined rows via HASH_GROUP_BY (node 2).

hypotheses.claim: UNION forces a deduplicating aggregate over both inputs. (matched: rips where trip_distance > 30 union select pulocationid, payment_type,)

HASH_GROUP_BY performs duplicate elimination for UNION DISTINCT; if the two result sets have high overlap, the hash table build/probe is wasteful and could be avoided with UNION ALL plus a downstream distinct or by rewriting to a single scan.
No indexes exist on trip_distance or fare_amount; adding a composite or single-column index on the filtered columns could turn the sequential scans into index scans if selectivity is high enough.
